decisions.reason: F2 attributed polynomial multiplicity and the localized DVR to a definition that only defines valuation rings. New step 1.1 constructs factor multiplicity, proves product and sum laws, extends it to F(t), and identifies the nonnegative ring with F[t] localized at (t-1). It also proves the field-characteristic consequences of F3. The zero Laurent difference is handled separately, and unit reduction is explicitly restricted to nonzero f. Frobenius gives the full p-power valuation; negative exponents are removed by units. Statement unchanged; Owning contract and manifest synchronized; final focused checks passed, including the batched layout check with zero defects.

The charged clause omitted f(z_1)=0 and therefore did not impose its promised quotient. Added the zero relation retaining both branches and boundaries. Direct consumer clauses already impose the zero polynomial, or use only the unchanged auxiliary affine presentation. During final hash validation a supplier interface changed; reread the current quantum-characteristic Definition, cyclic Cartan Definition and complete Verification, and generic Hecke Definition. They still give order e when q_H is not 1, characteristic e when q_H is 1, independent residue labels, dominant coefficients and level sum; the new rational weight form is irrelevant to this presentation. This actual supplier re-examination licenses the refreshed review context. Focused checks passed.

F3 attributed the Bruhat subword theorem to a supplier that states only the Coxeter presentation. The proof needs only minimum word length: a proper subword of k letters has at most k-1 letters and hence length below k. F3 now cites exactly the presentation, defines minimum length, and step 1.3 supplies this elementary estimate. The maximal-length crossed-product independence argument, integral spanning, anti-involution, localization, and base change are preserved; no Bruhat theorem or new prerequisite is needed. Statement unchanged; precheck and rendercheck passed.

The module-axiom definition supplies no submodule freeness over a DVR. Step 1.1 now proves it by coordinate induction: every nonzero coordinate ideal has a least valuation generator, its lift splits off one free summand, and the kernel has smaller ambient rank. Exactness is already proved by lifting and projecting in 1.3. F3 now separates the assumed standard basis and unitriangular submatrix from the defining Grothendieck relation; finite triangular elimination proves injectivity. Orthogonality, scalar-extended nondegeneracy and the leaf Gram identity give the claimed weight filtration, including rank zero. Statement unchanged; focused precheck and rendercheck passed.

The cited definitions give permutation invariance and primitive central idempotents, not elementary-symmetric generation or the nilpotent-ideal criterion. Added the characteristic-free leading-monomial elimination in step 1.2 and proved the idempotent criterion directly in step 2.1. Each content center is Fe plus a finitely generated nilpotent ideal with zero scalar intersection. A primitive central idempotent has exactly one nonzero content component, which is the entire primitive content idempotent. The split generalized projectors and symmetric-center equality remain hypotheses, with d=0 covered. Statement unchanged; precheck and rendercheck passed.

The unrestricted sums define global nilpotent dots, which can have nonzero components outside the named content sector. Restricting both sums to words of content alpha makes each element equal to e_alpha times its global counterpart and hence an element of e_alpha H e_alpha. On each word projector its dot is unchanged; finite orthogonality and the spectral supplier prove commuting nilpotence. Direct consumers use precisely these fixed-content restrictions or only the unchanged central idempotents; those uses remain sound. Rendercheck passed.

The title overstated the actual same-hub Statement: a strict size descent changes the sum of residue counts, so cannot preserve content. Changed only the display title to hub-preserving descent, retaining the stable ID and the richer same-hub switch Statement. Checked the margin parametrization, energy change 4-2gamma, Laplacian kernel, balanced-row minimum argument and binary-switch connectivity; they support the actual Statement. The fixed-content theorem F2 repeats the erroneous title-level attribution and is reported to its frontier owner; its fixed-rank lifts must preserve content, rather than the descending cores.

The supplier Statement supplies scalar normalizers and Hecke-side intertwiners, not a KLR-side faithful model or its Hecke coefficient table. Reproduced the five KLR operator braid patterns, the mixed/quadratic check and all six Hecke braid coefficients locally; added the actual Matsumoto and symmetric-group suppliers for crossing-word reduction. Leading permutation coefficients give faithfulness before quotient, so regular identities descend without inverting nilpotent dot differences. Checked both signs and the double edge against BK Theorems 3.3 and 4.3, reading pp. 13-17 and 24-27; their all-equal exercises are handled by the explicit divided-difference formula here. Statement and sector-factorization argument unchanged.

The claim that the matching first-residue factor is invertible off a joint word summand is false: complementary words can have the same first residue. Step 1.1 now cancels only other-residue factors within e(i), where distinct spectral values and nilpotent dots give explicit geometric-series inverses. The remaining matching factor is y_1 or a nonzero scalar multiple, proving the cyclotomic relation even when its exponent is zero. The normalized crossing products and five braid patterns agree with the supplied scalar identities and explicit affine calculations; the source all-equal case is checked by the displayed divided-difference antisymmetrizer. Statement unchanged; precheck and rendercheck passed.

The Laurent-parameter algebra in the defining supplier is multiplicative. Its z=1 specialization is not the charged additive degenerate algebra; the rank-one F_2 example distinguishes their idempotents. Made the application clause explicitly nondegenerate and added the presentation caveat, preserving the complete basis and cell law for every commutative unit-parameter specialization, including multiplicative z=1. This corrects the identification of an application rather than discarding a case of the defined H_n. Checked finite-generator straightening, the nonempty-component correction used for X_1, independent PBW rank and standard-pair count. Direct consumers use the same multiplicative H_n; the primitive-block theorem uses this result only in its q_H not equal to 1 branch.

Step 1.1 and F1 applied the component-start eigenvalue formula to empty components, where no node carries that putative eigenvalue. Restricted this intermediate calculation to nonempty components, exactly the cases selected by an actual tableau entry; the level-two lambda=(empty,(1)) counterexample now uses U_2 and makes no claim about U_1. The content-triangular Statement remains unchanged. Added the actual published Bruhat rank/subword supplier for the prefix comparison in step 2.1 rather than inheriting it from a Coxeter presentation. Initial internal labels, component shuffles and simultaneous triangular quotients give the stated node contents. Precheck and rendercheck passed.

The old Mackey count incorrectly omitted unflagged allocations from the full left cell. Step 1.3 constructs the component-shuffle tensor model and double-coset restriction, identifying the flagged subspace with flag-compatible allocations; 5.1 counts its trivial characters. The rejected lambda=mu=((1),(1)) has two full-cell allocations and one flagged allocation. Exact affine membership and literal Murphy coefficient identities retain arbitrary base change and unit pivots. Added the actual Bruhat supplier and removed unused F7/F8 facts; F4 supplies the generic ordinary multiplicities. Corrected F1 to call u_lambda a polynomial, not a unit. Consulted Mathas pp. 28-30 for the flag conventions, not an external proof fallback. Final precheck, rendercheck, contract, citation-fidelity, dependency and content-policy checks passed.

F5 added a nondegenerate-or-zero dichotomy absent from the cellular-basis supplier and false at singular parameters. Removed that added assertion while retaining the supplied bilinear forms. The proof of the actual generic Statement does not need it: distinct addable-node words separate shapes over both generic fields, cellular diagonal multiplicity one makes all Spechts simple, and the exact corner multiplicities make every Schur standard simple; its diagonal entry one makes the invariant form nonzero and hence nondegenerate. The bound on first-difference addable contents across components is below N, so the q_H t and Q_a t^(Na) words cannot collide. No singular-specialization nondegeneracy is claimed; Statement unchanged.

The transfer recipe did not specify charged beta positions; the ordinary runner f-1 ignores the receiving component charge and can produce a unit foot difference. Step 1.2 now defines B_c={lambda_j^(c)+c_c-j}, derives the charged foot formula, and moves the largest bead on charged runner f-1, equivalently uncharged runner f-c_b-1. The two different components force a unique hook pair, dominance comes from their order, equal charged residues give a nonzero difference of positive valuation, and the discrepancy-square descent terminates. In the rejected e=2, charges (0,1) example the receiver is (1,1), not (2), and its foot difference is t^2-t^3. Read LM Lemma 3.9 and its cross-component Proposition 3.6 argument, preserving all arbitrary-field hypotheses. Statement unchanged; precheck and rendercheck passed.

The original dimension obstruction lacked a positive-rank boundary. Qualified the title and proved the obstruction for every d at least one, retaining the rank-one witness: NG maps onto F[t,t^-1] by T_r=q_H and X_r=q_H^(r-1)t; DG maps onto F[t] by s_r=1 and x_r=t+(r-1). The quadratic, braid and mixed relations hold under these explicit assignments. Finite cyclotomic sectors and their KLR partners cannot be isomorphic to these infinite-dimensional affine algebras. At rank zero both algebras are F. The separate rank-two e=3 example still gives two one-dimensional blocks in F times F. Statement refuted unchanged; Final focused checks passed.
